answer: Give every agent identity a tamper-evident kernel: a hardware-backed birth certificate issued once per device at registration, like a passport office with limited counters. Each identity then writes its history with a signed quill — an append-only reputation ledger countersigned by unrelated peers, so fake clusters cannot self-certify. Finally, cap onboarding through a gale-throttled intake window: only a fixed number of new identities may enter per epoch, so a sybil flood can never outpace the verification queue and real agents keep working while fakes wait in line.
